retriever.query_prefix:
Instruct: Given a question about a long conversation between two people, retrieve the dialogue turns that help answer it.
Query:

data._comment: Pinned benchmark inputs. A number is only credible if the hash below matches what produced it. Changing any field invalidates every result already in results/.

locomo.restore: git clone https://github.com/snap-research/locomo data/locomo && git -C data/locomo checkout 3eb6f2c585f5e1699204e3c3bdf7adc5c28cb376
known_issues: Roughly 6.4% of gold answers are score-corrupting (benchmark audit, 2026). F1 is therefore a noisy ground truth, and single-run deltas below ~2 points are not interpretable.

A popular LoCoMo judge configuration accepted 62.8% of deliberately wrong answers (Penfield Labs, Apr 2026; non-peer-reviewed). This is why F1/EM is the headline metric here and judge scores are secondary.
The HuggingFace dataset 'adymaharana/locomo' is EMPTY. Always load from the GitHub repo.

VERIFIED 2026-10-18: the released locomo10.json does NOT use the paper's section 4.1 enumeration order. Real mapping: 1=multi-hop, 2=temporal, 3=open-domain, 4=single-hop, 5=adversarial -- from (a) evidence-turn structure (cat1 98% multi-evidence-turn, cat2 77% 'When ...', cat3 'Would ... likely' commonsense, cat4 95% single-turn, cat5 100% adversarial_answer) and (b) per-category proportions tracking paper Table 5 within a few points. See src/load.py CATEGORY_NAMES.

The paper scores the adversarial category with the same F1 and INCLUDES it in its Overall column, reporting Human=89.4 -- only possible if a correct refusal counts as a match. Its adversarial column is therefore refusal accuracy, and F1_paper (not F1) is the convention-matched number.
Table 3's Dialog k=10 multi-hop recall cell reads 247.4: impossible (>100%) and non-monotone against its neighbours (34.4 -> 247.4 -> 64.1 -> 75.5). Treat that cell as unusable.
Category 5 represents Abstention (_abs instances with false premises or unanswerable queries); scored as refusal accuracy matching LoCoMo Cat 5.
Community reports noted potential arithmetic discrepancies in a subset of temporal questions; see issue tracker.

pinned._comment: Measured properties of the serving stack, pinned like the dataset. These are not incidental: they bound which experiments are even valid, so they get the same treatment as provenance/datasets.json. Embedded whole into every manifest, which also means a run does not have to rely on env vars (LLM_SERVED_BY / LLM_QUANTIZATION) to record what served it.

effective_context_tokens.method: head/tail needle test. FIRST_MARKER=ALPHA7 at the very start of the prompt, LAST_MARKER=BETA9 at the very end, filler sized to ~2k / ~4k / ~8k tokens, asking the model to report both. At ~2000 and ~4000 tokens it returned FIRST=ALPHA7 LAST=BETA9. At ~8000 tokens it returned FIRST=<x> LAST=<BETA9>: the head was clipped, so the prompt was truncated from the front.
effective_context_tokens.consequence: k<=50 is safe (a k=50 context is ~2k tokens). `full` mode is NOT runnable: whole conversations are ~15k tokens and would be silently truncated from the front -- a `full` number would be an artifact. Do not report one until num_ctx is set explicitly and this test is re-run.
effective_context_tokens.why_not_declared: The model declares 32768, but ollama clamps the runtime num_ctx to its server default. Declared length is not effective length; only the test above settles it.

known_notes: Measured on a Colab free-tier Tesla T4. GPU model is recorded per run in the manifest's hardware block.
A fresh Colab runtime has no SSH key. Code is delivered as an uploaded git bundle, so no credential is ever placed on the VM. Do not reintroduce one.
